reason: Drove it and it reproduces exactly as stated, on both grounds and at both widths. Chromium, forcedColors:"active", owner-flight, editor opened on Send the invitations. LIGHT forced palette (Canvas #fff/CanvasText #000): pressed half computes background rgb(255,255,255) color rgb(0,0,0); unpressed computes rgba(255,255,255,0) color rgb(0,0,0). DARK forced palette (Canvas #000): pressed rgb(0,0,0)/white, unpressed transparent/white. border-width is 0px on the pressed half and 0px 0px 0px 1px on the other - that 1px is the divider, present regardless of which half is pressed. font-weight 400 on both. A 3x element capture of .b-seg shows two identical capsules: nothing on the control says which option is in force, and pressing Hidden changes nothing about the control. Same at 390x844. So the fill IS the entire state and the forced palette does erase it. Checks that could have killed it, and did not: (1) NOT a gate restatement. interaction-check.mjs has exactly one forced-colours block (~line 2105) and it asserts the rail, .b-todayRule and lead-vs-plain tick border only; .b-seg appears in the file at 519/543/927/1307/2094/2563/2767 for aria-pressed bookkeeping, undo strings, 44px targets and plate width - never for pressed APPEARANCE, in forced colours or out of it. audit.mjs runs with no forced palette. (2) NOT already handled, though it is partly mitigated and the finding overstates it. The row does carry the consequence: .b-item[data-visibility="hidden"] adds the words "Hidden from guests" (measured display:block, in view at both widths on both grounds) and a dashed tick border that the forced block leaves alone. But that is a 7px dot's 1px dash, and it is a readout of the consequence on a different object; there is no positive "shown" indicator anywhere, so the resting Shown state is only inferable from an absence. The control itself reports nothing either way. (3) NOT a constraint break: system-colour keywords resolve inside forced colours only, so no fourth hue reaches paper or ink; no weight, no architecture. (4) SETTLED.md carries nothing on forced colours or on .b-seg. (5) The block's own comment states the principle the omission violates - "a forced palette may repaint any fill, so the mark that means 'this one' is carried in geometry too" - and .b-seg is the only aria-pressed control on the surface, so it is genuinely the one stateful control the map skips. I applied the proposed fix at runtime and it works, but testing it turned up two things the finding did not know, one of which vindicates a line I was about to cut. FIRST: forced-color-adjust:none is NOT optional decoration - it is load-bearing. With `background: Highlight; color: HighlightText` alone (adjust left at auto), Chromium paints its forced-colours text backplate in Canvas behind the label, and HighlightText on that plate renders the word "Shown" as a solid white rectangle - measured and captured at 3x, the label is unreadable. With forced-color-adjust:none the same rule renders white-on-Highlight cleanly. Anyone sharpening this fix by dropping that line would ship a worse control than the one being fixed. SECOND, and the one correction the fix needs: forced-color-adjust:none also un-forces the global :focus-visible ring from shell.css:314 on the pressed half. Measured with real keyboard focus on the pressed button - light palette: outline rgb(79,70,229) with the fix versus rgb(55,0,110) without; dark palette: rgb(79,70,229) versus rgb(26,235,255). Author indigo on a black Canvas is about 2.6:1, and it would be the only focus ring on the surface that stops being a system colour. One extra declaration restores it. Real, specific, four lines, scoped to a media query neither shipping ground enters, and it closes the last hole in a map round 8 already paid for.
sharpenedFix: Take the fix as proposed, keeping forced-color-adjust:none (measured necessary - without it Chromium's text backplate swallows the label), and add one declaration to repair the focus ring that opting out breaks. Above the trailing @media block: .b-seg button { position: relative; }. Inside it: .b-seg button[aria-pressed="true"] { forced-color-adjust: none; background: Highlight; color: HighlightText; } .b-seg button[aria-pressed="true"]:focus-visible { outline-color: CanvasText; } .b-seg button[aria-pressed="true"]::after { content: ""; position: absolute; left: 6px; right: 6px; bottom: 3px; height: 2px; background: currentColor; } The focus rule is the correction: measured, adjust:none returns the ring to author indigo rgb(79,70,229) on both palettes, where the rest of the surface gets rgb(55,0,110) light / rgb(26,235,255) dark; outline-offset is 2px so the ring lands on Canvas, which makes CanvasText the right pair and restores black-on-white / white-on-black. Keep the ::after: currentColor resolves to HighlightText under adjust:none (black on cyan in a dark theme, white on purple in a light one), it costs nothing, and it applies to the segment the same reasoning the block already applies to the lead tick. Verify with two additions to interaction-check.mjs's existing forced-colours block: that the pressed half's background differs from the unpressed half's on both palettes, and that its computed outline-color under :focus-visible is not the author accent. Neither gate is touched otherwise - audit.mjs runs no forced palette, and position:relative changes no box, so the 44px target sweep at line 2094 is unaffected.
